rawIngestions.titleRaw: huggingface/transformers v5.23.0 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw: # Release v5.23.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling2 Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-small/) * Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in [#50682](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50682) ### JEV JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. `JevForDecision` is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (`head.safetensors` and `judge_config.json` for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental `decision` pipeline or directly with `decide`. **Note:** JEV and the decision pipeline are currently experimental. Their APIs, configuration, and behavior may change as development continues. They should be used with caution in production environments. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/jev) * Add Jev + decision core (#50054) by @ArthurZucker in [#50054](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50054) ### LFM3 LFM3 is the third generation of Liquid Foundation Models from Liquid AI. Like LFM2, it is a hybrid architecture that combines gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention, with the attention layers split between full-attention and sliding-window layers. The attention layers apply RMSNorm to the query and key heads and gate their output with a per-head sigmoid. Every layer applies a sandwich norm to the operator and feed-forward outputs before the residual addition. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lfm3) * [Model] LFM3 Family: LFM3-Text (#50322) by @paulpak58 in [#50322](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50322) ### Dots 3 Note Preview Dots 3 Note Preview is a mixture-of-experts causal language model that accepts native text, image, video, and audio inputs. It uses a shared vision encoder for images and videos and a Whisper-style audio encoder, and both encoders project their outputs into the language model's hidden space before autoregressive text generation. BF16 and FP8 inference are supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/dots3_note) * Add dots3-note Preview model support (#47844) by @miraclezqc in [#47844](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/47844) ### LFM3-VL LFM3-VL is a vision-language model family from Liquid AI, built on the LFM3 language model. It takes images and videos at their native resolution together with text. It combines a hybrid vision encoder (a linear patchifier, gated depthwise 2D convolution layers, and bidirectional grouped-query attention layers with 2D rotary embeddings) with a projector and an LFM3 language model. The projector merges each 2x2 block of patch features into one language token through a layer norm and a two-layer MLP. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lfm3_vl) * [Model] LFM3 Family: LFM3-VL (#50392) by @paulpak58 in [#50392](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50392) ### IQuestCoder IQuest-Coder-V1 is a family of code language models developed by IQuest Lab, available in 7B, 14B and 40B sizes with base, instruct and thinking variants. Its architecture is the same as Llama, so the Transformers auto classes load it with LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM, and only IQuestCoderConfig is specific to IQuestCoder. The looped `IQuest-Coder-V1-*-Loop-*` checkpoints use a different architecture and aren't supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/iquestcoder) * Add IQuestCoder (#50579) by @hmellor in [#50579](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50579) ### InternLM3 InternLM3 is an 8B instruction-tuned language model developed by Shanghai AI Laboratory (checkpoint: internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct). Its architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load it with the Llama implementation (LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM), and only InternLM3Config is specific to InternLM3. The config names the attention biases `qkv_bias` and the output projection and MLP biases `bias`. InternLM3Config loads these as `attention_bias` and `mlp_bias` and requires them to be equal, as they are in the released checkpoints. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/internlm3) * Add InternLM3 (#50578) by @hmellor in [#50578](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50578) ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Remove the `ep_router` expert-parallel style (#49615) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Run MXFP4 GPT-OSS experts through `ep_dispatch_experts` (#49613) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 `deepgemm_megamoe` EP implementation for DeepGEMM Mega MoE (#49606) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Slim down `[audio]` to torchaudio + soundfile + soxr (drop librosa and phonemizer) (#50610) by @eustlb * 🚨 Deprecate Wav2Vec2ProcessorWithLM and pyctcdecode/kenlm LM decoding (#50408) by @eustlb * 🚨 Exporters: `ExportedModel`, Hub save/load, one backend registry (#50029) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Move processing defaults to class (#49089) by @guarin * :rotating_light: [`kernels`] Bump version (#50307) by @vasqu * :rotating_light: Finally drop rope deltas from ModelOutput! (#50153) by @zucchini-nlp * 🚨 Safe-ize pi0 graphs (#50160) by @molbap * 🚨 [serve][breaking] update attn for mac users (#49730) by @SunMarc * 🚨 build and expand once the tp/ep_plan/fsdp_plan (#49527) by @3outeille ## Exporters: export, share and run any model on its backend (#50029, #50032, #50309, #50311) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b17b2ab-b2b8-4e34-a983-4a7177330e4e Every export now returns an `ExportedModel`. You call it like the original model (same kwargs, same output class), push it to the Hub, and load it back on the backend's own runtime. The same API covers Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch. ```python from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer from transformers.exporters import ExportedModel, OnnxConfig, OnnxExporter model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2") tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2") inputs = tokenizer(["Exporters are here!"], return_tensors="pt") exported = OnnxExporter().export(model, inputs, OnnxConfig(dynamic=True, ort_fusions="cuda")) exported.push_to_hub("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx") exported_model = ExportedModel.from_pretrained("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx", device="cuda") outputs = exported_model(**inputs) # same output class as model(**inputs) ``` - **Fused for the runtime**: `OnnxConfig(ort_fusions="cpu" | "cuda" | "webgpu" | "dml")` rewrites the graph into ONNX Runtime's fused transformer ops at export time: attention, `GroupQueryAttention` over the KV cache, rotary, norms and `MoE`. OpenVINO exports now hit OpenVINO's fused CPU kernels for attention, RoPE, MoE experts and compressed int8/int4 weights, which makes decode 2.4–3.9× faster than before. - **Faster than `torch.compile`**: on EmbeddingGemma2 (8 × 128 tokens), ONNX Runtime with the TensorRT EP is 7.6× faster than eager PyTorch and 1.4× faster than `torch.compile` on an A100. OpenVINO is 4.1× faster than eager and 2.2× faster than `torch.compile` on a Xeon Platinum 8570 (4.9× and 2.6× with int8 weights). - **Shareable**: an export saves and loads like a model, optionally in a `subfolder` of the model repo. Its `export.json` records the config, input shapes, package versions and I/O names. Quantized exports (PT2E, NNCF, ONNX Runtime) save and run the same way. 🚨 `export()` returns an `ExportedModel`, and an ONNX program is an `onnx_ir.Model`. `OnnxConfig`'s and `OpenVINOConfig`'s `output_path` options are gone in favour of `save_pretrained`. Custom backends register with `register_backend`. 📚 Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/exporters ## Vision This release fixes a range of vision-model bugs: classification pipelines now respect `problem_type`, and several models get corrected behavior (Step3.7 RoPE axis order, MiniMax-M3-VL packed attention isolation, Qwen VL positions with reused caches, PaddleOCR-VL interpolation alignment, Kosmos2 SDPA masking, and Emu3 float image handling). release.body: # Release v5.23.0 ## New Model additions ### Inkling2 Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/inkling2) | [Blog Post](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-small/) * Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in [#50682](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50682) ### JEV JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. `JevForDecision` is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (`head.safetensors` and `judge_config.json` for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental `decision` pipeline or directly with `decide`. **Note:** JEV and the decision pipeline are currently experimental. Their APIs, configuration, and behavior may change as development continues. They should be used with caution in production environments. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/jev) * Add Jev + decision core (#50054) by @ArthurZucker in [#50054](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50054) ### LFM3 LFM3 is the third generation of Liquid Foundation Models from Liquid AI. Like LFM2, it is a hybrid architecture that combines gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention, with the attention layers split between full-attention and sliding-window layers. The attention layers apply RMSNorm to the query and key heads and gate their output with a per-head sigmoid. Every layer applies a sandwich norm to the operator and feed-forward outputs before the residual addition. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lfm3) * [Model] LFM3 Family: LFM3-Text (#50322) by @paulpak58 in [#50322](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50322) ### Dots 3 Note Preview Dots 3 Note Preview is a mixture-of-experts causal language model that accepts native text, image, video, and audio inputs. It uses a shared vision encoder for images and videos and a Whisper-style audio encoder, and both encoders project their outputs into the language model's hidden space before autoregressive text generation. BF16 and FP8 inference are supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/dots3_note) * Add dots3-note Preview model support (#47844) by @miraclezqc in [#47844](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/47844) ### LFM3-VL LFM3-VL is a vision-language model family from Liquid AI, built on the LFM3 language model. It takes images and videos at their native resolution together with text. It combines a hybrid vision encoder (a linear patchifier, gated depthwise 2D convolution layers, and bidirectional grouped-query attention layers with 2D rotary embeddings) with a projector and an LFM3 language model. The projector merges each 2x2 block of patch features into one language token through a layer norm and a two-layer MLP. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/lfm3_vl) * [Model] LFM3 Family: LFM3-VL (#50392) by @paulpak58 in [#50392](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50392) ### IQuestCoder IQuest-Coder-V1 is a family of code language models developed by IQuest Lab, available in 7B, 14B and 40B sizes with base, instruct and thinking variants. Its architecture is the same as Llama, so the Transformers auto classes load it with LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM, and only IQuestCoderConfig is specific to IQuestCoder. The looped `IQuest-Coder-V1-*-Loop-*` checkpoints use a different architecture and aren't supported. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/iquestcoder) * Add IQuestCoder (#50579) by @hmellor in [#50579](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50579) ### InternLM3 InternLM3 is an 8B instruction-tuned language model developed by Shanghai AI Laboratory (checkpoint: internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct). Its architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load it with the Llama implementation (LlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM), and only InternLM3Config is specific to InternLM3. The config names the attention biases `qkv_bias` and the output projection and MLP biases `bias`. InternLM3Config loads these as `attention_bias` and `mlp_bias` and requires them to be equal, as they are in the released checkpoints. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/internlm3) * Add InternLM3 (#50578) by @hmellor in [#50578](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50578) ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Remove the `ep_router` expert-parallel style (#49615) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Run MXFP4 GPT-OSS experts through `ep_dispatch_experts` (#49613) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 `deepgemm_megamoe` EP implementation for DeepGEMM Mega MoE (#49606) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Slim down `[audio]` to torchaudio + soundfile + soxr (drop librosa and phonemizer) (#50610) by @eustlb * 🚨 Deprecate Wav2Vec2ProcessorWithLM and pyctcdecode/kenlm LM decoding (#50408) by @eustlb * 🚨 Exporters: `ExportedModel`, Hub save/load, one backend registry (#50029) by @IlyasMoutawwakil * 🚨 Move processing defaults to class (#49089) by @guarin * :rotating_light: [`kernels`] Bump version (#50307) by @vasqu * :rotating_light: Finally drop rope deltas from ModelOutput! (#50153) by @zucchini-nlp * 🚨 Safe-ize pi0 graphs (#50160) by @molbap * 🚨 [serve][breaking] update attn for mac users (#49730) by @SunMarc * 🚨 build and expand once the tp/ep_plan/fsdp_plan (#49527) by @3outeille ## Exporters: export, share and run any model on its backend (#50029, #50032, #50309, #50311) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b17b2ab-b2b8-4e34-a983-4a7177330e4e Every export now returns an `ExportedModel`. You call it like the original model (same kwargs, same output class), push it to the Hub, and load it back on the backend's own runtime. The same API covers Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO and ExecuTorch. ```python from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer from transformers.exporters import ExportedModel, OnnxConfig, OnnxExporter model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2") tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google/embeddinggemma-2") inputs = tokenizer(["Exporters are here!"], return_tensors="pt") exported = OnnxExporter().export(model, inputs, OnnxConfig(dynamic=True, ort_fusions="cuda")) exported.push_to_hub("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx") exported_model = ExportedModel.from_pretrained("my-org/embeddinggemma-2-onnx", device="cuda") outputs = exported_model(**inputs) # same output class as model(**inputs) ``` - **Fused for the runtime**: `OnnxConfig(ort_fusions="cpu" | "cuda" | "webgpu" | "dml")` rewrites the graph into ONNX Runtime's fused transformer ops at export time: attention, `GroupQueryAttention` over the KV cache, rotary, norms and `MoE`. OpenVINO exports now hit OpenVINO's fused CPU kernels for attention, RoPE, MoE experts and compressed int8/int4 weights, which makes decode 2.4–3.9× faster than before. - **Faster than `torch.compile`**: on EmbeddingGemma2 (8 × 128 tokens), ONNX Runtime with the TensorRT EP is 7.6× faster than eager PyTorch and 1.4× faster than `torch.compile` on an A100. OpenVINO is 4.1× faster than eager and 2.2× faster than `torch.compile` on a Xeon Platinum 8570 (4.9× and 2.6× with int8 weights). - **Shareable**: an export saves and loads like a model, optionally in a `subfolder` of the model repo. Its `export.json` records the config, input shapes, package versions and I/O names. Quantized exports (PT2E, NNCF, ONNX Runtime) save and run the same way. 🚨 `export()` returns an `ExportedModel`, and an ONNX program is an `onnx_ir.Model`. `OnnxConfig`'s and `OpenVINOConfig`'s `output_path` options are gone in favour of `save_pretrained`. Custom backends register with `register_backend`. 📚 Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/exporters ## Vision This release fixes a range of vision-model bugs: classification pipelines now respect `problem_type`, and several models get corrected behavior (Step3.7 RoPE axis order, MiniMax-M3-VL packed attention isolation, Qwen VL positions with reused caches, PaddleOCR-VL interpolation alignment, Kosmos2 SDPA masking, and Emu3 float image handling). Chunked prefill now keeps image inputs on the * fix(pipelines): respect problem_type in image and video classification pipelines (#50582) by @surendra902 in [#50582] * Fix Step3.7 vision RoPE spatial W/H axis order (#50547) by @caohch-1 in [#50547] * Raise ValueError for out-of-range float images in convert_to_rgb (#50487) by @n24q02m in [#50487] * CI: install OpenVINO and NNCF in the daily GPU image (#50422) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#50422] * Fix MiniMax-M3-VL packed vision attention isolation (#50346) by @taking-lying-flat in [#50346] * Fix Qwen VL positions when a text cache is reused with a new image (#50427) by @Arnav66692 in [#50427] * [Docker] Update Nvidia CI and Flash Attn CI images to torch 2.15 / cu132 (#50467) by @ydshieh in [#50467] * Fix PaddleOCR-VL vision position interpolation alignment (#50384) by @scyyh11 in [#50384] * Fix Emu3 image processor crash on float numpy images (#50226) by @simpleqt in [#50226] * Build Idefics-style vision position ids with torch.where (#49917) by @shoumikhin in [#49917] * Keep image inputs on the first chunk of a chunked prefill (#49753) by @digit50 in [#49753] * Docs: note in the v5 migration guide that hidden_states[-1] of vision models is pre-norm (#50303) by @ravediamond in [#50303] * Remove the GitHub API cache-bust from the AMD docker images (#49351) by @tarekziade in [#49351] * [docs] Vision backend differences (#50131) by @stevhliu in [#50131] * [Kosmos2] Fix SDPA applying a causal mask in the image-to-text projection (#50118) by @tarekziade in [#50118] ## Parallelization This release improves distributed training and inference. Expert parallelism gains a selectable `ep_implementation` (all-reduce for CUDA-graph-friendly inference, all-to-all for training). The Trainer now reduces FSDP/HSDP gradients only on the last micro-batch, and the token-count normalization is fixed to use true division. Tensor-parallel fixes cover attention sinks (including Beam attention) and tied-weight comparisons on TPU * Expert-parallel implementations for `ep_dispatch_experts`: all-reduce at inference, all-to-all in training (#49429) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49429] * [FSDP tests] Fork CPU ranks from a forkserver instead of spawning them (#50444) by @ydshieh in [#50444] * [distributed - TPU] Fix tied-weight comparisons on TPUs when using TP (#50406) by @tengomucho in [#50406] * [`distributed`] Trainer: reduce FSDP/HSDP gradients on the last micro-batch only (#50286) by @3outeille in [#50286] * Update FSDP non-rank-0 missing keys test after #45649 (#50260) by @SunMarc in [#50260] * [`Beam`] Fix TP on attn (#50302) by @vasqu in [#50302] * Fix/trainer parallel token count 50212 (#50214) by @BlazeSR10hawk in [#50214] * Reuse the TP/EP test ranks across tests instead of spawning them per test (#49986) by @3outeille in [#49986] * handle local sink in TP (#49567) by @3outeille in [#49567] ## Cache This release fixes several cache correctness issues: static-cache prefill attention in Gemma4's KV-shared layers, Qwen VL positions when a cache is reused with a new image or video, and DeepSeek-V4 compression-state reordering during beam search. It also improves cache sharing for Mistral Large 4 and adds OpenVINO export fusion for the KV cache and attention. Smaller changes cover CI and test fixes, including vLLM CI memory * Gemma4: fix static cache attending to empty cache slots in KV-shared layers at prefill (#50528) by @ydshieh in [#50528] * vLLM CI: fix install and KV-cache memory, add failure report job (#50436) by @ydshieh in [#50436] * Fix DeepSeek-V4 compression cache reordering for beam search (#50348) by @taking-lying-flat in [#50348] * OpenVINO exporter: let OpenVINO fuse attention, RoPE, the KV cache and compressed matmuls (#50311) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#50311] * [tests] Pin the chat-template date in Llama's FA static-cache test (#50296) by @tarekziade in [#50296] * Fix a cache test (#50320) by @Cyrilvallez in [#50320] * Improve Mistral Large 4 cache sharing (#50305) by @Cyrilvallez in [#50305] ## Kernels This release fixes several hub kernel issues: the MPS RMSNorm kernel repo id was corrected, the MegaBlocksMoeMLP mapping was restored for MXFP4 GPT-OSS, and a failed flash-attention kernel load is now retried instead of leaving models unregistered. It also raises the minimum `kernels` version (fixing ROCm issues and a multi-GPU bug), bumps mamba-ssm kernels to v4 * Fix the MPS RMSNorm hub kernel repo id (#50714) by @tarekziade in [#50714] * [`GptOss`] Fix the kernels autodispatch test (#50630) by @vasqu in [#50630] * [`kernels`] Bump min version (#50509) by @vasqu in [#50509] * Retry the attention kernel load after a failed `lazy_import_flash_attention` (#50391) by @albertvillanova in [#50391] * Test the dispatched FA3 kernel per device (#50304) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in [#50304] * upgrade version for mamba-ssm and fla kernel (#50294) by @kaixuanliu in [#50294] * Restore the `MegaBlocksMoeMLP` hub kernel mapping for MXFP4 GPT-OSS (#50150) by @jiqing-feng in [#50150] ## Attention This release fixes a range of attention bugs: vision-attention isolation in MiniMax-M3-VL, SDPA decode under `torch.compile`, eager NaNs in Qwen4-Exp with left padding, an unintended causal mask in Kosmos-2's SDPA projection, and default full-attention mask selection that wrongly picked linear layers. It also retries failed attention kernel loads, excludes padding from the repetition penalty, and lets the O * [`SDPA`] Fix decode under compile (#50388) by @vasqu in [#50388] * Exclude attention-masked padding from repetition penalty (#50149) by @BlazeSR10hawk in [#50149] * Fix Qwen4-Exp eager attention NaNs with left padding (#49923) by @taking-lying-flat in [#49923] * [Masking] Skip linear layers for the default full-attention mask (#50059) by @paulpak58 in [#50059] ## Generation This release fixes several generation bugs: padded generation in RecurrentGemma, batched decoding in Falcon-H1, beam search cache reordering in DeepSeek-V4, and batched metadata and beam scores in `TextGenerationPipeline`. It also lets an unchanged `GenerationConfig` be saved without strict-validation errors, avoids copying the KV cache when decoding with grouped-query attention (GQA), and fixes an `Attribut * Fix RecurrentGemma padded generation by declaring its `layer_types` (#50577) by @ydshieh in [#50577] * Fix Falcon-H1 gated RMSNorm shape during batched decoding (#50507) by @taking-lying-flat in [#50507] * Allow saving an unchanged generation config (#49914) by @benthecarman in [#49914] * Fold GQA query heads onto their KV head when decoding instead of repeating K/V (#49743) by @Yooniel in [#49743] * fix(pipelines): preserve batched generation metadata (#50210) by @BlazeSR10hawk in [#50210] * Fix AttributeError on LinearAttentionLayer in export generate test (#50140) by @ydshieh in [#50140] ## Quantization This release fixes several quantization bugs: FP8 `modules_to_not_convert` entries are now renamed like weight names, so modules such as `f_a_proj` and `f_b_proj` are no longer wrongly quantized. MXFP4 experts now dequantize to the requested dtype instead of always using bfloat16. rawIngestions.titleRaw: ollama/ollama v0.40.17 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
## Inkling 2 Mini
[Inkling 2 Mini](https://ollama.com/library/inkling-2-mini) from Thinking Machines is a 26B parameter model with 5.4B active.

Its looped layers give it more computation per token than its size suggests, and it still fits on a Mac at about 20GB. It handles text and images, tool calls, and thinking, and scores 79.2% on SWE-Bench Verified).

```
  ollama run inkling-2-mini
```

Note: inkling-2-mini is supported on Apple silicon only in this release.  PC support will follow in an upcoming release.

 ## What's Changed
- `ollama launch claude` supports Claude Code's deferred tool loading, so MCP tools are loaded when needed instead of all at
once
- Ollama on Apple silicon now serves multiple requests at once.
- `ollama launch opencode` sets thinking options from the model's metadata
- `ollama launch pi` refreshes Pi's model list after sign-in and passes along prompt arguments
- `ollama launch chatgpt --restore` asks before switching an active profile and preserves existing settings and chat history;
 quitting ChatGPT yourself now lets it exit through its own quit prompt
- Running `ollama` with no arguments in a non-interactive shell prints help instead of erroring
- Ctrl+C or Ctrl+G while in a multiline `"""` block leaves multiline mode instead of swallowing the next line
- Changing the context shift setting no longer reloads the model
- Vulkan now uses mmap for integrated GPUs, fixing `Failed to allocate pinned memory` load failures on shared-memory GPUs
- On Windows iGPUs, partially offloaded models no longer fail to allocate the KV cache
- Tool definitions passed through the API keep JSON schema keywords Ollama doesn't model instead of dropping them
- Disabling thinking now maps to the model's lowest supported reasoning level rather than being ignored
- Source builds can use prebuilt MLX-C and XGrammar binaries

    **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.16...v0.40.17-rc3

rawIngestions.titleRaw: ollama/ollama v0.40.15 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
## MiMo V2.6

Xiaomi MiMo's [mimo-v2.6](https://ollama.com/library/mimo-v2.6), a 9B model built for code and agent workflows, is now supported in Ollama.

```sh
ollama run mimo-v2.6
```

## AutoTrust decision models

[AutoTrust](https://ollama.com/library/autotrust-jev) decision models read text and return choices, yes or no probabilities, and ratings for the questions you supply. The family includes 9b, 35b, and 27b-vl sizes — the 35b and 27b-vl sizes can also read images.

```sh
ollama run autotrust-jev "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

Note: autotrust-jev is supported on Apple silicon in this release.

## What's Changed

 - ollama launch now supports Kimi Code CLI — the successor to kimi-cli — and offers to migrate existing kimi-cli setups
 - ollama launch now fills in Pi's model list automatically so models can be picked inside Pi, and Claude Desktop's model
   picker shows Ollama's actual model names
 - Recurrent and vision GGUF models can now serve more than one request at a time
 - Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models using long-context (YaRN) scaling
 - Running ollama with no arguments opens the welcome launcher

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.14...v0.40.15

rawIngestions.titleRaw: ollama/ollama v0.40.14 released
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
## What's Changed
* `ollama launch claude` now applies the model's output token limit for Claude Code, so cloud models no longer run into the 128k default cap
* Cloud web search responses on `/api/chat` are now decoded correctly, including compressed responses
* OpenAI-compatible endpoints no longer override a model's packaged sampler defaults — clients that send no `temperature`/`top_p` get the model's own values instead of 1.0, matching `/api/chat`
* `/v1/responses` now preserves readable input content, including prior assistant refusals, instead of flattening it
* Ollama's app can now retry ChatGPT disconnect failures instead of leaving the connection in a broken state
* `ollama launch codex` verifies ChatGPT routing before configuring, and reports a clear error when routing is unavailable
* Faster top-k sampling on MLX for large vocabularies

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.13...v0.40.14

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Show HN: AgentState – Lightweight state manager for multi-agent AI workflows
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
AgentState to solve a problem I kept running into: managing state for multi-agent AI systems is surprisingly hard. When you have multiple AI agents that need to coordinate, persist their state, and query each other's status, you typically end up with a mess of Redis/Postgres setups, custom queuing, and manual synchronization code.

The whole thing is ~3MB, written in Rust for performance and safety, runs in Docker, and handles 1000+ ops/sec. I've been running it in production for AI workflows and it's been rock solid.

rawIngestions.titleRaw: Show HN: ML Blocks – Deploy multimodal AI workflows without code
rawIngestions.contentRaw:
Hey everyone,

ML Blocks is a node-based workflow builder to create multi-modal AI workflows without writing any code.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.

predictions.rationale: This signal matters because it changes how teams in operations can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance. This signal matters because it changes how teams in strategy can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance.
predictions.aiDraft: Customer AI is evolving from content generation into guided action orchestration.
predictions.analystRevision: Watch for stronger products to attach policy logic, queue routing, and recommended follow-up steps to the summarization layer.

predictions.title: Multimodal systems will unlock more operational AI in physical workflows
predictions.statement: Within 180 days, multimodal AI will show more durable value in inspection, field service, and documentation-heavy physical workflows than in generic consumer demos.
predictions.rationale: This signal matters because it changes how teams in product can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance. This signal matters because it changes how teams in Research can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance.
predictions.aiDraft: Multimodal systems are becoming more valuable when tied to messy physical operations rather than novelty experiences.
predictions.analystRevision: The practical win condition here is better documentation, faster triage, and stronger human review in workflows that already blend text, image, or voice.

predictions.title: AI intelligence products will differentiate through structured analyst framing
predictions.statement: Within 90 days, AI monitoring products that combine structured data, business framing, and prediction discipline will stand out more than products that only aggregate links.
predictions.rationale: This signal matters because it changes how teams in strategy can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance. This signal matters because it changes how teams in engineering can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance.
predictions.aiDraft: Information products are moving up the stack from aggregation to judgment and prioritization.
predictions.analystRevision: Aggregation is table stakes. Durable differentiation is more likely to come from prioritization, business interpretation, and explicit reasoning about implications.

predictions.title: Document-heavy workflows will remain among the clearest near-term AI ROI categories
predictions.statement: Within 180 days, document-heavy workflows such as legal review, procurement analysis, and compliance monitoring will continue to outperform novelty AI use cases on measurable ROI.
predictions.rationale: This signal matters because it changes how teams in strategy can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance. This signal matters because it changes how teams in engineering can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance.
predictions.aiDraft: Structured document workflows remain one of the best operational fits for enterprise AI.
predictions.analystRevision: These workflows keep winning because the source material is repetitive, the review loop is clear, and the business bottleneck is easy to measure.

predictions.title: Support AI will evolve from summarization to action orchestration
predictions.statement: Within 30 days, support-focused AI announcements will increasingly bundle summarization with routing, policy checks, and escalation recommendations.
predictions.rationale: Support use cases are already shifting toward workflow action layers instead of isolated content generation.
predictions.aiDraft: Support copilots are likely to move from note-taking into full queue and escalation orchestration.
predictions.analystRevision: Watch for support products that attach policy routing and recommended actions to conversation summaries.

predictions.title: AI tooling stacks will fragment before they consolidate
predictions.statement: Over the next 30 days, more teams will add specialized AI plugins and point tools before later consolidating around a smaller approved workflow stack.
predictions.rationale: Signals show rapid plugin specialization in VS Code and broader pressure to standardize later for risk and workflow clarity.
predictions.aiDraft: The next stage of adoption is likely to be short-term tool sprawl followed by stack consolidation.
predictions.analystRevision: This looks like a temporary fragmentation phase: experimentation first, workflow governance second.

predictions.title: Workflow orchestration will become the core design layer for operational AI
predictions.statement: Within 90 days, more AI systems will be evaluated on how well they coordinate tasks, memory, review, and handoffs across workflows instead of on isolated one-step outputs.
predictions.rationale: This signal matters because it changes how teams in operations can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance. This signal matters because it changes how teams in engineering can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance.
predictions.aiDraft: Operational value is converging around orchestration quality rather than single-response capability.
predictions.analystRevision: The strongest AI products will increasingly look like workflow systems with AI inside them, not AI demos with thin wrappers.

predictions.title: Structured outputs will become a default requirement for operational AI
predictions.statement: Within 180 days, structured output support and schema validation will be treated as baseline requirements for operational AI deployments.
predictions.rationale: Structured outputs are increasingly central to integrating AI into automation, analytics, and reporting systems safely.
predictions.aiDraft: Schema-safe outputs are likely to move from nice-to-have to baseline requirement in enterprise AI workflows.
predictions.analystRevision: Organizations that treat LLM output as system input will force structured output reliability into the default feature set for vendor selection.

predictions.title: Analyst workflows will adopt AI fastest where final judgment remains visible
predictions.statement: Over the next 90 days, analyst and strategy teams will adopt AI more aggressively in memo drafting and synthesis than in fully autonomous recommendation systems.
predictions.rationale: Signals emphasize human-in-the-loop synthesis and judgment support rather than decision replacement.
predictions.aiDraft: Analyst-centered workflows favor decision support over autonomous recommendation generation.
predictions.analystRevision: The strongest adoption pattern will be 'AI drafts, humans decide' in research, strategy, and business analysis environments.

predictions.title: AI intelligence products will differentiate through analyst framing
predictions.statement: Within 90 days, AI monitoring products that add clear business interpretation and analyst framing will stand out more than products that only aggregate links.
predictions.rationale: Information abundance is no longer the constraint; meaning, relevance, and business interpretation are the scarce layer.
predictions.aiDraft: The most valuable AI news products will likely combine aggregation with business interpretation.
predictions.analystRevision: Aggregation is table stakes; judgment, prioritization, and business framing are the durable differentiators.

reports.executiveSummary: Today's AI picture is being shaped by open-source stack, frontier research, customer operations. The strongest signals point to a market where research progress, platform controls, and workflow execution are converging into more operational buying criteria.
strategicTakeaways: The open-source layer is turning into a strategic option set for AI stack design, not only a hobbyist ecosystem.
Research matters most when it changes the product and deployment baseline, not only leaderboard positioning.
Customer operations AI is shifting from note-taking to controlled action recommendation and orchestration.
reports.businessImpactSummary: This signal matters because it changes how teams in operations can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance. This signal matters because it changes how teams in strategy can structure AI-assisted execution, evaluation, or governance.
predictionUpdates: Research progress will matter most when it changes deployment economics and evaluation standards
Platform competition will shift toward reliability, controls, and integration depth
Open-source AI infrastructure will compress time-to-prototype for serious teams

reports.executiveSummary: Today's AI market signal is broader than any single vendor or coding tool. Research progress, platform controls, open-source infrastructure, and workflow-specific applications are converging into a new execution layer for business and product teams.
strategicTakeaways: Research and platform releases increasingly matter when they change deployment economics, evaluation standards, or workflow reliability.
Structured outputs and action permissioning are becoming non-negotiable for enterprise AI operations.
The biggest moat may belong to teams that own workflow integration, analyst framing, and operational context, not model access alone.
reports.businessImpactSummary: Business teams should treat AI less like a feature race and more like a workflow design decision. The winners will be organizations that combine model capability with governance, review systems, and domain-specific execution patterns.
predictionUpdates: Workflow continuity remains a strong differentiator, but it now sits alongside governance, retrieval quality, and open-stack flexibility.
Permission design is emerging as a practical gate for enterprise agent deployment.
Analyst-reviewed intelligence products may become more valuable than pure AI news aggregation.

reports.executiveSummary: The AI product layer continues to move closer to execution. Today's strongest signals center on production evals, governance, knowledge systems, and workflow categories where AI can take on repeatable synthesis or coordination tasks.
strategicTakeaways: Production evals are moving into the foreground for enterprise agent design.
Permissioned action tiers offer a clearer path to trusted automation.
Support and operations are becoming orchestration-heavy AI categories.
reports.businessImpactSummary: Operators should expect workflow governance and measurable control layers to become buying criteria for enterprise AI stacks.
predictionUpdates: Support AI is likely to move beyond summarization into routing and action orchestration.
Structured outputs and evals are becoming operational infrastructure.

reports.executiveSummary: AI productivity platforms are competing less on novelty and more on how smoothly they fit into existing developer, analyst, and operational workflows.
strategicTakeaways: Editor-native workflows matter more than standalone copilots.
Review and context continuity are key adoption drivers.
Engineering teams need stack clarity before tool sprawl gets expensive.
reports.businessImpactSummary: Developer platform decisions increasingly look like workflow architecture decisions, not one-off tool purchases.
predictionUpdates: Tool fragmentation will likely precede a consolidation phase.
